svg.title: Airworthiness Directives (ADs): what they are and how compliance is recorded
svg.desc: ADs under 14 CFR part 39 require correction of unsafe conditions likely to exist in other products of the same design. Two categories: emergency, with immediate compliance before further flight, and less urgent, with compliance within a specified period. ADs are regulatory and must be complied with unless a specific exemption is granted. No overflying of an AD hour limit unless the AD says so. Section 91.417 requires a record of method of compliance, AD number and revision date, next due date and time, and the signature, certificate type and certificate number of the person who did the work.
svg.text: Airworthiness Directives (ADs): what they are and how compliance is recorded
Under 14 CFR part 39 the FAA requires correction of unsafe conditions found in an aircraft, engine,
propeller or appliance.
An unsafe condition exists and is likely to exist or develop in other products of the same design. It
may come from a design defect, maintenance, or other causes. ADs notify owners and other interested
persons and specify the conditions under which the product may continue to be operated.
Two categories
Emergency nature
Requires immediate compliance prior to further flight
Less urgent nature
Requires compliance within a specified period of time
They are regulatory
ADs shall be complied with unless a specific
exemption is granted
The aircraft owner or operator must ensure
compliance with all pertinent ADs, including
those requiring recurrent or continuing action
Example: an AD may require a repetitive
inspection each 50 hours of operation; it shall
be accomplished and recorded every 50 hours of
time in service
There is no provision to overfly the maximum hour
requirement of an AD unless it is specifically
written into the AD
Where to find them
All ADs and the AD Biweekly are free on the
Internet at http://rgl.faa.gov and available
through e-mail
The Summary of Airworthiness Directives has all
valid ADs published; small aircraft and
helicopter books cover aircraft of 12,500 pounds
or less
Placards may be reproduced as directed by an AD
The Handling, Service, and Maintenance section
notes that ADs can require additional maintenance
or inspections
Recording compliance (14 CFR part 91, section 91.417): the AD status record
Method of compliance
AD number and revision date, if recurring
Next due date and time
Signature (repair station or mechanic)
Type of certificate
Certificate number
The record is made by the repair station or mechanic who performed the work. For ready reference, many owners
keep a chronological list of the pertinent ADs in the back of the aircraft, engine and propeller maintenance
records.
